{{Short description|German mathematician}}
'''Theodor Schönemann''', also written '''Schoenemann''' (4 April 1812{{spaced ndash}}16 January 1868), was a German mathematician who obtained several important results in [[number theory]] concerning the theory of [[Modular arithmetic|congruences]], which can be found in several publications in [[Crelle's Journal|Crelle's journal]], volumes 17 to 40.  Notably, he obtained [[Hensel's lemma]] before [[Kurt Hensel|Hensel]], [[Scholz's reciprocity law]] before Scholz, and formulated [[Eisenstein's criterion]] before [[Gotthold Eisenstein|Eisenstein]].<ref>David A. Cox, "Why Eisenstein proved the Eisenstein criterion and why Schönemann discovered it first", [[American Mathematical Monthly]] '''118''' Vol 1, January 2011, pp. 3–31. The mentioned statement is on p.&nbsp;13.</ref> He also studied, under the form of integer polynomials [[ideal (ring theory)|modulo]] both a [[prime number]] and an [[irreducible polynomial]] (remaining irreducible modulo that prime number), what can nowadays be recognized as [[finite field]]s (more general than those of prime order).<ref>David A. Cox, "Why Eisenstein proved the Eisenstein criterion and why Schönemann discovered it first", [[American Mathematical Monthly]] '''118''' Vol 1, January 2011, pp. 3–31. See p.&nbsp;10.</ref>

He was educated in [[Königsberg]] and Berlin, where among his teachers were [[Jakob Steiner]] and [[Carl Gustav Jacob Jacobi]]. He obtained his doctorate in 1842, after which he became Gymnasialoberlehrer (professor at a gymnasium) in [[Brandenburg an der Havel]]. Apart from the mentioned mathematical papers, he also published, mainly after 1850, in mechanics and physical technique.

== Works ==
* ''Ueber die Bewegung veränderlicher ebener Figuren, welche während der Bewegung sich ähnlich bleiben in ihrer Ebene''. 1862 [http://nbn-resolving.de/urn:nbn:de:hbz:061:1-107823 digital]
